diagrams.subtitle: Eukaryotic cellular system coordinating respiration, protein packaging, and genetic governance

licence.source: NIH 3D Model 3DPX-015797 via Cell Architecture Studio
licence.creator: National Institutes of Health (NIH 3D Exchange) & Cell Architecture Studio
licence.attribution: 3D specimen based on verified anatomical NIH 3D model 3DPX-015797 via Cell Architecture Studio.

structures.name: Mitochondrion
structures.description: Double-membraned organelle with folded inner cristae housing the electron transport chain.
structures.function: Site of aerobic cellular respiration where pyruvate is broken down in the presence of oxygen to synthesize ATP molecules.

structures.name: Nucleus
structures.description: Large spherical organelle enclosed by a porous double nuclear membrane containing chromatin and DNA.
structures.function: Stores chromosomes, directs cellular metabolic activities, transcription, and division.

structures.name: Golgi Apparatus
structures.description: Stack of flattened, membrane-bound cisternae with distinct cis and trans faces.
structures.function: Modifies, sorts, packages, and tags proteins and lipids into vesicles for delivery inside or outside the cell.

pathways.name: Aerobic Cellular Respiration Flow
pathways.description: Glycolysis in cytoplasm followed by oxidative phosphorylation in mitochondria

assessments.prompt: Identify the double-membraned organelle where aerobic respiration occurs to release chemical energy stored as ATP.
assessments.hint: Often termed the 'powerhouse of the cell' with folded inner cristae.

assessments.prompt: Explain the difference in ATP yield and cellular location between aerobic respiration and anaerobic glycolysis.
rubric_points: Glycolysis occurs in the cytoplasm and yields only 2 ATP per glucose molecule without oxygen
Aerobic respiration occurs inside mitochondria in the presence of oxygen
Mitochondrial breakdown of pyruvate yields high ATP (up to 36-38 ATP per glucose)
Aerobic respiration produces carbon dioxide and water as harmless end products

diagrams.subtitle: Photosynthetic eukaryotic cell featuring cellulose cell wall, chloroplasts, and turgor-regulating vacuole

licence.creator: Cell Architecture Studio
licence.attribution: Plant cell architecture and GLB asset from Cell Architecture Studio open educational assets.

structures.name: Cell Wall
structures.description: Rigid outer protective layer composed of cellulose microfibrils providing mechanical tensile strength.
structures.function: Provides structural shape, prevents osmotic lysis when water enters, and maintains plant upright posture.

structures.name: Chloroplast
structures.description: Double-membraned photosynthetic plastids containing chlorophyll pigment within stacked thylakoids.
structures.function: Site of photosynthesis: chlorophyll absorbs light photons, splits water molecules (photolysis) to release oxygen, and reduces carbon dioxide into glucose.

structures.name: Central Vacuole
structures.description: Enormous fluid-filled central compartment enclosed by the tonoplast membrane, occupying most of mature plant cell volume.
structures.function: Maintains turgor pressure against the cell wall, stores cell sap containing nutrients, and keeps non-woody plants firm.

structures.name: Nucleus
structures.description: Double-membrane spherical organelle pushed toward the cell periphery by the expansive central vacuole.
structures.function: Governs cellular metabolism, transcription, and holds nuclear DNA encoding plant developmental enzymes.

pathways.name: Photosynthetic Energy Conversion
pathways.description: Light absorption in chloroplast thylakoids yielding glucose stored in cytoplasm and vacuole

assessments.prompt: Identify the green double-membraned organelle where chlorophyll absorbs solar photons to split water molecules during photosynthesis.
assessments.hint: Contains stacked thylakoids and chlorophyll pigments giving plants their green appearance.

assessments.prompt: Explain why plant cells possess a rigid outer cell wall and large central vacuole, whereas animal cells do not.
rubric_points: Cell wall prevents osmotic bursting (lysis) when plant cells absorb water by osmosis
Central vacuole creates turgor pressure pressing against the rigid wall to keep herbaceous plants upright
Animals have skeletal support and locomotive mobility so they do not require rigid cellular walls
Vacuole serves as a large storage reservoir for cell sap, amino acids, and water

diagrams.subtitle: Excitable neural cell specialized for unidirectional electrical impulse conduction and synaptic signaling

licence.source: NIH 3D Model 3DPX-015796 via Cell Architecture Studio
licence.creator: National Institutes of Health (NIH 3D Exchange) & Cell Architecture Studio
licence.attribution: Neuron 3D specimen from verified NIH 3D model 3DPX-015796 via Cell Architecture Studio.

structures.name: Dendrites
structures.description: Highly branched protoplasmic tree-like extensions emanating from the neuronal soma.
structures.function: Detects chemical and physical environmental stimuli or neurotransmitters from upstream neurons, generating an initial electrical impulse.

structures.name: Soma (Cell Body)
structures.description: Central bulbous portion of the neuron containing a prominent spherical nucleus and mitochondria.
structures.function: Metabolic maintenance center integrating incoming dendritic electrical potentials and funnelling action potentials into the axon.

structures.name: Axon
structures.description: Elongated, slender cylindrical projection extending from the cyton toward terminal arborizations.
structures.function: Conducts electrical action potentials rapidly and unidirectionally away from the cyton toward target synapses.

pathways.name: Unidirectional Nerve Impulse Pathway
pathways.description: Electrochemical conduction from sensory dendritic tip through soma to axon terminal release

assessments.prompt: Identify the branched extensions of the neuron that receive incoming chemical signals and initiate the electrical nerve impulse.
assessments.hint: Branching arborizations protruding directly from the cell body.

assessments.prompt: Arrange the neural components in the strict physiological order that a nerve impulse travels through a single neuron.
assessments.hint: Impulse travels unidirectionally from the receiving tips to the conducting fiber.

assessments.prompt: Explain why the transmission of a nerve impulse across a chemical synapse is strictly unidirectional.
rubric_points: Synaptic vesicles containing neurotransmitters are present exclusively in the axon terminals of the presynaptic neuron
Neurotransmitter receptors are located exclusively on the dendritic membrane of the postsynaptic neuron
Chemical messengers can only diffuse across the synaptic cleft from terminal to dendrite, never in reverse
This structural asymmetry ensures electrical signaling follows an orderly, non-colliding circuit

diagrams.subtitle: Single-celled prokaryotic organism with peptidoglycan wall, flagellar motor, and nucleoid chromosome

licence.source: NIH 3D Model 3DPX-010752 via Cell Architecture Studio
licence.creator: National Institutes of Health (NIH 3D Exchange) & Cell Architecture Studio
licence.attribution: Gram-positive bacterial cell wall specimen from verified NIH 3D model 3DPX-010752 via Cell Architecture Studio.

structures.name: Peptidoglycan Cell Wall
structures.description: Rigid meshwork composed of polysaccharide chains cross-linked by short amino acid peptides.
structures.function: Maintains bacterial cell shape, prevents osmotic lysis in aqueous hypotonic environments, and protects against host defenses.

structures.name: Nucleoid (Bacterial Chromosome)
structures.description: Irregularly shaped region within prokaryotic cytoplasm containing circular double-stranded DNA not enclosed by a membrane.
structures.function: Carries the essential genetic instructions governing bacterial metabolism, binary fission, and enzymatic synthesis.

structures.name: Bacterial Flagellum
structures.description: Helical filament composed of flagellin protein embedded in a rotary motor complex driven by proton motive force.
structures.function: Rotates at high speeds to propel the bacterium towards nutrients (chemotaxis) and away from noxious substances.

pathways.name: Prokaryotic Cell Boundary & Motility
pathways.description: Cell wall protective barrier coordinates with rotary flagellar motor

assessments.prompt: Identify the cytoplasm region containing the circular bacterial genetic material that lacks a surrounding nuclear envelope.
assessments.hint: The naked DNA region characteristic of prokaryotes.

assessments.prompt: Explain the major structural differences between a prokaryotic bacterium and a eukaryotic animal cell.
rubric_points: Prokaryotes lack a membrane-bound nucleus; their DNA floats freely in the nucleoid region
Prokaryotes lack membrane-bound organelles such as mitochondria and Golgi apparatus
Bacteria possess a rigid cell wall composed of peptidoglycan, whereas animal cells have no cell wall
Bacterial ribosomes are 70S compared to eukaryotic 80S cytoplasmic ribosomes

diagrams.subtitle: Specialized motile immune cell featuring lobed nucleus, digestive lysosomes, and defensive granules

licence.creator: Cell Architecture Studio
licence.attribution: Immune cell morphology and GLB asset from Cell Architecture Studio open educational assets.

structures.name: Lobed Nucleus
structures.description: Multi-segmented flexible nucleus interconnected by thin chromatin strands.
structures.function: Provides structural malleability, allowing the leucocyte to deform and migrate through endothelial junctions (diapedesis) into infected tissue.

structures.name: Lysosome
structures.description: Enzyme-filled membrane vesicles fusing with phagosomes to form phagolysosomes.
structures.function: Degrades and digests engulfed pathogenic bacteria, cellular debris, and foreign antigens using acidic hydrolases.

structures.name: Antimicrobial Granules
structures.description: Cytoplasmic storage vesicles packed with defensins, lysozyme, and myeloperoxidase.
structures.function: Releases bactericidal enzymes to destroy invading microorganisms and signal inflammatory mediators.

pathways.name: Phagocytosis & Intracellular Killing Flow
pathways.description: Pathogen recognition followed by phagolysosome degradation and granule degranulation

assessments.prompt: Identify the flexible multi-lobed cellular organelle that enables white blood cells to squeeze through blood capillary walls.
assessments.hint: Multi-segmented nucleus specialized for cellular deformability and diapedesis.

assessments.prompt: Explain the biological importance of diapedesis and phagocytosis in human defense against bacterial infections.
rubric_points: Diapedesis allows white blood cells to squeeze between capillary endothelial cells to reach infected tissue sites
Phagocytosis allows white blood cells to engulf and destroy invading pathogenic bacteria
Lysosomes fuse with the ingested vesicle to degrade microbes with hydrolytic enzymes
Antimicrobial granules discharge bactericidal enzymes to neutralize pathogens

diagrams.subtitle: Polarized tissue cell lining mucosal surfaces featuring apical microvilli brush border and tight junction seals

licence.creator: Cell Architecture Studio
licence.attribution: Procedural columnar epithelial architecture from Cell Architecture Studio.

structures.name: Microvilli
structures.description: Dense microscopic finger-like protoplasmic projections packed on the apical cell surface.
structures.function: Dramatically expands surface area (brush border) for rapid absorption of digested nutrients, water, and ions.

structures.name: Tight Junctions
structures.description: Continuous belt-like multiprotein complexes sealing the intercellular space between adjacent cells.
structures.function: Forms a selectively impermeable barrier preventing paracellular leakage and maintaining epithelial cell polarity.

structures.name: Nucleus
structures.description: Oval diploid nucleus positioned toward the basal cytoplasm of the columnar epithelial cell.
structures.function: Stores genetic blueprints, orchestrating protein synthesis for digestive enzymes and transport carrier channels.

pathways.name: Transcellular Nutrient Absorption Flow
pathways.description: Apical uptake across microvilli brush border into basal vascular transport

assessments.prompt: Identify the apical brush border projections that dramatically expand cellular surface area for nutrient absorption.
assessments.hint: Microscopic hair-like projections lining intestinal and renal epithelial cells.

assessments.prompt: Explain how tight junctions preserve epithelial barrier integrity and prevent paracellular leakage in the intestinal lining.
rubric_points: Tight junctions form an occluding seal between neighboring epithelial plasma membranes
Prevent uncontrolled paracellular diffusion of digestive enzymes and pathogens into internal tissues
Preserve cellular polarity by separating apical transport proteins from basolateral channels
Forces nutrients to traverse selectively via regulated transcellular absorption

diagrams.subtitle: Elongated multinucleated contractile fiber packed with repeating sarcomere myofibrils and mitochondria

licence.creator: Cell Architecture Studio
licence.attribution: Procedural skeletal muscle fiber architecture from Cell Architecture Studio.

structures.name: Myofibril
structures.description: Cylindrical contractile organelles composed of repeating sarcomere units of actin and myosin myofilaments.
structures.function: Shortens via sliding filament mechanism during muscle contraction, generating mechanical force and body movement.

structures.name: Sarcolemma
structures.description: Specialized excitable plasma membrane enclosing the multinucleated muscle fiber.
structures.function: Propagates electrical action potentials along the fiber surface and down transverse T-tubules to trigger calcium release.

structures.name: Mitochondria
structures.description: Numerous energy-converting organelles densely packed between parallel myofibril bundles.
structures.function: Continuously synthesizes ATP to fuel myosin head detachment and calcium pumping during repeated muscular contraction.

pathways.name: Excitation-Contraction Coupling Flow
pathways.description: Membrane excitation across sarcolemma activating myofibril shortening fueled by mitochondrial ATP

assessments.prompt: Identify the contractile filament bundles exhibiting repeating sarcomere striations that shorten to generate muscular force.
assessments.hint: Cylindrical protein threads packed with actin and myosin.

assessments.prompt: Explain why muscle cells require high mitochondrial density and describe the anaerobic pathway in human muscle during vigorous exercise.
rubric_points: Muscular contraction consumes high quantities of ATP for cross-bridge cycling and calcium reuptake
High mitochondrial density ensures continuous aerobic ATP synthesis under normal oxygen supply
During vigorous exercise when oxygen delivery is insufficient, muscle cells switch to anaerobic glycolysis
Pyruvate is converted to lactic acid in cytoplasm, yielding only 2 ATP per glucose and leading to muscle fatigue and cramps
